title: SAML account linking creates transient duplicate principals leading to role bloat and inconsistent deny checks
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Summary: Several customer escalations reported two related symptoms after a recent SSO/SAML attribute sync change: (1) users saw intermittent "permission denied" errors even though they were members of an admin group; (2) in other cases, accounts accumulated extra permissions (role bloat) when SAML-linked identities created transient duplicate principals during rapid provisioning/sync. Root cause appears to be a race between SAML assertion-based linking and the background group-sync job plus ambiguous provenance of role grants in the RBAC v2 model. The system currently merges roles on link without recording source provenance and applies allow-rules before deny precedence resolution in some enforcement paths. We need a fix that prevents over-permissioning, makes audit trails explicit for link/unlink and role merges, and reconciles deny/allow evaluation order across sync paths.
acceptance_criteria: SAML-based link flow produces a single canonical principal per external identity in >99.99% of test runs (no duplicates in 10k synthetic link attempts)
Background sync and on-assertion linking are serialized or idempotent such that role merges include provenance tags and can be reversed safely

Authorization checks evaluate explicit denies with precedence across all enforcement paths (assertion-time, cached token time, background sync) and no customer can gain an admin role without an audit event recorded
Audit log schema contains event types: saml.link, saml.unlink, rbac.role_grant (with provenance and correlation_id), and saml.sync.conflict and is searchable in Kibana/dashboard
E2E tests covering fast parallel SAML assertions and group-sync demonstrate no permission-denied regressions and no role-bloat in 99.999 percentile of runs
proposed_solution: 1) Canonicalization: compute canonical_principal_id from SAML NameID + tenant-id at assertion handler entry. Use single CREATE/GET DB operation with unique constraint to avoid duplicates. 2) Provenance: extend role_grants table with a provenance string and correlation_id (migration) to record whether grant came from 'saml:assertion', 'saml:sync', 'admin-console', etc. 3) Precedence: change enforcement logic to always check explicit deny flags (deny-list, explicit deny grants) before allow merges; unify evaluation code paths (runtime enforcer + cache layer + background reconciliation) to call a single evaluator function. 4) Safe merge: when merging roles on link, attach provenance, and avoid automatic elevation to admin unless a manual or authoritative source is present. 5) Audit: emit structured audit events on link/unlink and role changes with the correlation_id propagated through the request chain. 6) Mitigation: temporary feature-flag that disables automatic role-merge during SAML sync for affected customers while fix is deployed.
tradeoffs_and_notes: DB migration to add provenance increases row size and requires careful index planning; estimated migration time 10m-30m on prod primary. We'll add the column nullable and backfill asynchronously to reduce migration window.

Unifying enforcement paths requires touching cache eviction and enforcer code in three services (auth-runner, realtime-cache, background-sync). Risk of regressions — will gate behind canary deploys and increased tracing.
Temporary mitigation (disable auto-merge) increases friction for orgs that expect immediate group changes after SSO; tradeoff accepted to reduce privilege escalation risk.
We may see a small latency increase (~2-5ms p95) when adding provenance propagation and correlation IDs to auth paths; acceptable given security priority.
Security review is required because this changes deny/allow semantics and audit surfaces; coordinate with legal/compliance for customers with strict audit requirements.
implementation_plan: Week 0: Reproduce with a deterministic test harness that simulates 1000 parallel SAML assertions and background sync operations (owner: Ravi)
Week 1: Add canonicalization DB uniqueness and simple lockless upsert for principal linking; add integration test (owner: Ravi)
Week 2: Add provenance column + migration plan; implement audit event emitters for saml.link and rbac.role_grant (owner: infra+auth)
Week 3: Update enforcer common library to enforce explicit-deny precedence; update cache invalidation logic (owner: auth-runtime)
Week 4: Canary deploy to internal staging, run chaos tests that introduce delayed syncs and dropped assertions; roll back on failures (owner: SRE)
Hotfix: Feature-flag to disable auto-merge for customers reporting incidents; document customer opt-out and rollout steps (owner: Support/PM)
Post-deploy: Run backfill job to populate provenance for recent role grants and run audit-query to validate (owner: data-engineering)
Follow-up: Create a lightweight UI in Console to show link provenance for org admins (next cycle, owner: Console)
Docs: Confluence write-up with sequence diagrams and mitigations; link included below

links: Kibana query: saml.link OR rbac.role_grant (saved search)
testing_plan: Unit tests for canonical upsert and provenance field population
Integration test: simulate 10k parallel SAML assertions against staging cluster with background sync enabled
E2E: role evaluation tests including explicit deny scenarios across cache, runtime and background sync paths
Canary: deploy to 5% of requests plus single-tenant canary for affected customers, monitor audit events and permission-denied rate
Post-deploy: run backfill and run a regression query to ensure no role_bloat events for the last 7 days
risks: Migration risk: adding a provenance column requires careful rollout to avoid long locks on the role_grants table
Regression risk: changing enforcement order could unintentionally block legitimate access if provenance tags are missing for older grants
Customer discomfort: disabling auto-merge may temporarily break onboarding for some orgs
Operational: correlation_id propagation requires updates to multiple services and could be missed in async pipelines
